title: Which Foods Have Gluten, and Which Are Naturally Gluten-Free?

seo.title: Foods With Gluten and Naturally Gluten-Free Foods
seo.meta_description: Wheat, barley, and rye contain gluten. Rice, corn, potatoes, quinoa, beans, produce, plain meat, fish, eggs, and dairy are naturally gluten-free.
seo.search_intent: Identify gluten-containing foods and foods that are naturally free of gluten.

excerpt: Gluten is found in wheat, barley, rye, and their related varieties or derivatives. Rice, corn, potatoes, quinoa, beans, fruits, vegetables, plain meat, fish, eggs, and dairy are naturally gluten-free, but processed foods can add gluten ingredients or cross-contact.
content_html:
A gluten-free diet does not mean avoiding every grain. Gluten is a group of proteins found primarily in wheat, barley, and rye, while many familiar foods never contain it naturally.

The grains that require attention

Wheat and wheat relatives such as spelt and durum contain gluten, as do barley and rye. Bread, pasta, couscous, bulgur, conventional beer, malt, and many breaded foods come from these grains.

Naturally gluten-free food is a long list

Rice, corn, potatoes, quinoa, buckwheat, millet, and legumes are naturally gluten-free. So are fruits, vegetables, plain meat, fish, eggs, milk, oils, and plain nuts.

Processing can change the answer

Sauces, deli meats, soups, desserts, seasoned potatoes, and other prepared products can include wheat ingredients or encounter cross-contact. For celiac disease, a gluten-free label and careful handling matter.

Under FDA rules, foods labeled gluten-free must contain less than 20 parts per million of gluten. The food's natural source is the first filter; labeling and cross-contact are the second.

faq.question: Is quinoa gluten-free?
faq.answer: Yes, naturally, although people with celiac disease should still consider cross-contact in processed products.

faq.question: What does gluten-free mean on a U.S. label?
faq.answer: FDA requires a labeled gluten-free food to contain less than 20 parts per million of gluten.
